[112](https://docs.rs#112)/// See [`Client::add_chain`].
[113](https://docs.rs#113)#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
[114](https://docs.rs#114)pub struct AddChainConfig<'a, TChain, TRelays> {
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    /// Opaque user data that the [`Client`] will hold for this chain. Can later be accessed using
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    /// the `Index` and `IndexMut` trait implementations on the [`Client`].
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    pub user_data: TChain,
[118](https://docs.rs#118)
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    /// JSON text containing the specification of the chain (the so-called "chain spec").
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    pub specification: &'a str,
[121](https://docs.rs#121)
[122](https://docs.rs#122)    /// Opaque data containing the database content that was retrieved by calling
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    /// the `chainHead_unstable_finalizedDatabase` JSON-RPC function in the past.
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    ///
[125](https://docs.rs#125)    /// Pass an empty string if no database content exists or is known.
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    ///
[127](https://docs.rs#127)    /// No error is generated if this data is invalid and/or can't be decoded. The implementation
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    /// reserves the right to break the format of this data at any point.
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    pub database_content: &'a str,
[130](https://docs.rs#130)
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    /// If [`AddChainConfig`] defines a parachain, contains the list of relay chains to choose
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    /// from. Ignored if not a parachain.
[133](https://docs.rs#133)    ///
[134](https://docs.rs#134)    /// This field is necessary because multiple different chain can have the same identity. If
[135](https://docs.rs#135)    /// the client tried to find the corresponding relay chain in all the previously-spawned
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    /// chains, it means that a call to [`Client::add_chain`] could influence the outcome of a
[137](https://docs.rs#137)    /// subsequent call to [`Client::add_chain`].
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    ///
[139](https://docs.rs#139)    /// For example: if user A adds a chain named "Kusama", then user B adds a different chain
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    /// also named "Kusama", then user B adds a parachain whose relay chain is "Kusama", it would
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    /// be wrong to connect to the "Kusama" created by user A.
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    pub potential_relay_chains: TRelays,
[143](https://docs.rs#143)
[144](https://docs.rs#144)    /// Configuration for the JSON-RPC endpoint.
[145](https://docs.rs#145)    pub json_rpc: AddChainConfigJsonRpc,
[146](https://docs.rs#146)
[147](https://docs.rs#147)    /// If `Some`, enables the statement store networking protocol.
[148](https://docs.rs#148)    pub statement_protocol_config: Option<network_service::StatementProtocolConfig>,
[149](https://docs.rs#149)}
[150](https://docs.rs#150)
[151](https://docs.rs#151)/// See [`AddChainConfig::json_rpc`].
[152](https://docs.rs#152)#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
[153](https://docs.rs#153)pub enum AddChainConfigJsonRpc {
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    /// No JSON-RPC endpoint is available for this chain.  This saves up a lot of resources, but
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    /// will cause all JSON-RPC requests targeting this chain to fail.
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    Disabled,
[157](https://docs.rs#157)
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    /// The JSON-RPC endpoint is enabled. Normal operations.
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    Enabled {
[160](https://docs.rs#160)        /// Maximum number of JSON-RPC requests that can be added to a queue if it is not ready to
[161](https://docs.rs#161)        /// be processed immediately. Any additional request will be immediately rejected.
[162](https://docs.rs#162)        ///
[163](https://docs.rs#163)        /// This parameter is necessary in order to prevent JSON-RPC clients from using up too
[164](https://docs.rs#164)        /// much memory within the client.
[165](https://docs.rs#165)        /// If the JSON-RPC client is entirely trusted, then passing `u32::MAX` is
[166](https://docs.rs#166)        /// completely reasonable.
[167](https://docs.rs#167)        ///
[168](https://docs.rs#168)        /// A typical value is 128.
[169](https://docs.rs#169)        max_pending_requests: NonZero<u32>,
[170](https://docs.rs#170)
[171](https://docs.rs#171)        /// Maximum number of active subscriptions that can be started through JSON-RPC functions.
[172](https://docs.rs#172)        /// Any request that causes the JSON-RPC server to generate notifications counts as a
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        /// subscription.
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        /// Any additional subscription over this limit will be immediately rejected.
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        ///
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        /// This parameter is necessary in order to prevent JSON-RPC clients from using up too
[177](https://docs.rs#177)        /// much memory within the client.
[178](https://docs.rs#178)        /// If the JSON-RPC client is entirely trusted, then passing `u32::MAX` is
[179](https://docs.rs#179)        /// completely reasonable.
[180](https://docs.rs#180)        ///
[181](https://docs.rs#181)        /// While a typical reasonable value would be for example 64, existing UIs tend to start
[182](https://docs.rs#182)        /// a lot of subscriptions, and a value such as 1024 is recommended.
[183](https://docs.rs#183)        max_subscriptions: u32,
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    },
[185](https://docs.rs#185)}
[186](https://docs.rs#186)
[187](https://docs.rs#187)/// Chain registered in a [`Client`].
[188](https://docs.rs#188)///
[189](https://docs.rs#189)/// This type is a simple wrapper around a `usize`. Use the `From<usize> for ChainId` and
[190](https://docs.rs#190)/// `From<ChainId> for usize` trait implementations to convert back and forth if necessary.
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//
[192](https://docs.rs#192)// Implementation detail: corresponds to indices within [`Client::public_api_chains`].
[193](https://docs.rs#193)#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
[194](https://docs.rs#194)pub struct ChainId(usize);
[195](https://docs.rs#195)
[196](https://docs.rs#196)impl From<usize> for ChainId {
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    fn from(id: usize) -> ChainId {
[198](https://docs.rs#198)        ChainId(id)
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    }
[200](https://docs.rs#200)}
[201](https://docs.rs#201)
[202](https://docs.rs#202)impl From<ChainId> for usize {
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    fn from(chain_id: ChainId) -> usize {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)        chain_id.0
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    }
[206](https://docs.rs#206)}
[207](https://docs.rs#207)
[208](https://docs.rs#208)/// Holds a list of chains, connections, and JSON-RPC services.
[209](https://docs.rs#209)pub struct Client<TPlat: platform::PlatformRef, TChain = ()> {
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// Access to the platform capabilities.
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    platform: TPlat,
[212](https://docs.rs#212)
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    /// List of chains currently running according to the public API. Indices in this container
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    /// are reported through the public API. The values are either an error if the chain has failed
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    /// to initialize, or key found in [`Client::chains_by_key`].
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    public_api_chains: slab::Slab<PublicApiChain<TPlat, TChain>>,
[217](https://docs.rs#217)
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    /// De-duplicated list of chains that are *actually* running.
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    ///
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    /// For each key, contains the services running for this chain plus the number of public API
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    /// chains that correspond to it.
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    ///
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    /// Because we use a `SipHasher`, this hashmap isn't created in the `new` function (as this
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    /// function is `const`) but lazily the first time it is needed.
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    chains_by_key: Option<HashMap<ChainKey, RunningChain<TPlat>, util::SipHasherBuild>>,
[226](https://docs.rs#226)
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    /// All chains share a single networking service created lazily the first time that it
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    /// is used.
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    network_service: Option<Arc<network_service::NetworkService<TPlat>>>,
[230](https://docs.rs#230)}
[231](https://docs.rs#231)
[232](https://docs.rs#232)struct PublicApiChain<TPlat: PlatformRef, TChain> {
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    /// Opaque user data passed to [`Client::add_chain`].
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    user_data: TChain,
[235](https://docs.rs#235)
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    /// Index of the underlying chain found in [`Client::chains_by_key`].
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    key: ChainKey,
[238](https://docs.rs#238)
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    /// Identifier of the chain found in its chain spec. Equal to the return value of
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    /// [`chain_spec::ChainSpec::id`]. Used in order to match parachains with relay chains.
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    chain_spec_chain_id: String,
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    /// Handle that sends requests to the JSON-RPC service that runs in the background.
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    /// Destroying this handle also shuts down the service. `None` iff
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    /// [`AddChainConfig::json_rpc`] was [`AddChainConfigJsonRpc::Disabled`] when adding the chain.
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    json_rpc_frontend: Option<json_rpc_service::Frontend<TPlat>>,
[247](https://docs.rs#247)
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    /// Notified when the [`PublicApiChain`] is destroyed, in order for the [`JsonRpcResponses`]
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    /// to detect when the chain has been removed.
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    public_api_chain_destroyed_event: event_listener::Event,
[251](https://docs.rs#251)}
[252](https://docs.rs#252)
[253](https://docs.rs#253)/// Identifies a chain, so that multiple identical chains are de-duplicated.
[254](https://docs.rs#254)///
[255](https://docs.rs#255)/// This struct serves as the key in a `HashMap<ChainKey, ChainServices>`. It must contain all the
[256](https://docs.rs#256)/// values that are important to the logic of the fields that are contained in [`ChainServices`].
[257](https://docs.rs#257)/// Failing to include a field in this struct could lead to two different chains using the same
[258](https://docs.rs#258)/// [`ChainServices`], which has security consequences.
[259](https://docs.rs#259)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[260](https://docs.rs#260)struct ChainKey {
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// Hash of the genesis block of the chain.
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    genesis_block_hash: [u8; 32],
[263](https://docs.rs#263)
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    // TODO: what about light checkpoints?
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    // TODO: must also contain forkBlocks, and badBlocks fields
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    /// If the chain is a parachain, contains the relay chain and the "para ID" on this relay
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    /// chain.
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    relay_chain: Option<(Box<ChainKey>, u32)>,
[269](https://docs.rs#269)
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// Networking fork id, found in the chain specification.
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    fork_id: Option<String>,
[272](https://docs.rs#272)}
[273](https://docs.rs#273)
[274](https://docs.rs#274)struct RunningChain<TPlat: platform::PlatformRef> {
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    /// Services that are dedicated to this chain. Wrapped within a `MaybeDone` because the
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    /// initialization is performed asynchronously.
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    services: ChainServices<TPlat>,
[278](https://docs.rs#278)
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    /// Name of this chain in the logs. This is not necessarily the same as the identifier of the
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    /// chain in its chain specification.
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    log_name: String,
[282](https://docs.rs#282)
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    /// Number of elements in [`Client::public_api_chains`] that reference this chain. If this
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    /// number reaches `0`, the [`RunningChain`] should be destroyed.
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    num_references: NonZero<u32>,
[286](https://docs.rs#286)}
[287](https://docs.rs#287)
[288](https://docs.rs#288)struct ChainServices<TPlat: platform::PlatformRef> {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    network_service: Arc<network_service::NetworkServiceChain<TPlat>>,
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    sync_service: Arc<sync_service::SyncService<TPlat>>,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    runtime_service: Arc<runtime_service::RuntimeService<TPlat>>,
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    transactions_service: Arc<transactions_service::TransactionsService<TPlat>>,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    bitswap_service: Arc<bitswap_service::BitswapService>,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)}
[295](https://docs.rs#295)
[296](https://docs.rs#296)impl<TPlat: platform::PlatformRef> Clone for ChainServices<TPlat> {
[297](https://docs.rs#297)    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
[298](https://docs.rs#298)        ChainServices {
[299](https://docs.rs#299)            network_service: self.network_service.clone(),
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            sync_service: self.sync_service.clone(),
[301](https://docs.rs#301)            runtime_service: self.runtime_service.clone(),
[302](https://docs.rs#302)            transactions_service: self.transactions_service.clone(),
[303](https://docs.rs#303)            bitswap_service: self.bitswap_service.clone(),
[304](https://docs.rs#304)        }
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    }
[306](https://docs.rs#306)}
[307](https://docs.rs#307)
[308](https://docs.rs#308)/// Returns by [`Client::add_chain`] on success.
[309](https://docs.rs#309)pub struct AddChainSuccess<TPlat: PlatformRef> {
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    /// Newly-allocated identifier for the chain.
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    pub chain_id: ChainId,
[312](https://docs.rs#312)
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    /// Stream of JSON-RPC responses or notifications.
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    ///
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    /// Is always `Some` if [`AddChainConfig::json_rpc`] was [`AddChainConfigJsonRpc::Enabled`],
[316](https://docs.rs#316)    /// and `None` if it was [`AddChainConfigJsonRpc::Disabled`]. In other words, you can unwrap
[317](https://docs.rs#317)    /// this `Option` if you passed `Enabled`.
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    pub json_rpc_responses: Option<JsonRpcResponses<TPlat>>,
[319](https://docs.rs#319)}
[320](https://docs.rs#320)
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// Stream of JSON-RPC responses or notifications.
[322](https://docs.rs#322)///
[323](https://docs.rs#323)/// See [`AddChainSuccess::json_rpc_responses`].
[324](https://docs.rs#324)pub struct JsonRpcResponses<TPlat: PlatformRef> {
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    /// Receiving side for responses.
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    ///
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    /// As long as this object is alive, the JSON-RPC service will continue running. In order
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    /// to prevent that from happening, we destroy it as soon as the
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    /// [`JsonRpcResponses::public_api_chain_destroyed`] is notified of the destruction of
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    /// the sender.
[331](https://docs.rs#331)    inner: Option<json_rpc_service::Frontend<TPlat>>,
[332](https://docs.rs#332)
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    /// Notified when the [`PublicApiChain`] is destroyed.
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    public_api_chain_destroyed: event_listener::EventListener,
[335](https://docs.rs#335)}
[336](https://docs.rs#336)
[337](https://docs.rs#337)impl<TPlat: PlatformRef> JsonRpcResponses<TPlat> {
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    /// Returns the next response or notification, or `None` if the chain has been removed.
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    pub async fn next(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)        if let Some(frontend) = self.inner.as_mut() {
[341](https://docs.rs#341)            if let Some(response) = futures_lite::future::or(
[342](https://docs.rs#342)                async { Some(frontend.next_json_rpc_response().await) },
[343](https://docs.rs#343)                async {
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                    (&mut self.public_api_chain_destroyed).await;
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                    None
[346](https://docs.rs#346)                },
[347](https://docs.rs#347)            )
[348](https://docs.rs#348)            .await
[349](https://docs.rs#349)            {
[350](https://docs.rs#350)                return Some(response);
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            }
[352](https://docs.rs#352)        }
[353](https://docs.rs#353)
[354](https://docs.rs#354)        self.inner = None;
[355](https://docs.rs#355)        None
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    }
[357](https://docs.rs#357)}
[358](https://docs.rs#358)
[359](https://docs.rs#359)impl<TPlat: platform::PlatformRef, TChain> Client<TPlat, TChain> {
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    /// Initializes the smoldot client.
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    pub const fn new(platform: TPlat) -> Self {
[362](https://docs.rs#362)        Client {
[363](https://docs.rs#363)            platform,
[364](https://docs.rs#364)            public_api_chains: slab::Slab::new(),
[365](https://docs.rs#365)            chains_by_key: None,
[366](https://docs.rs#366)            network_service: None,
[367](https://docs.rs#367)        }
[368](https://docs.rs#368)    }
[369](https://docs.rs#369)
[370](https://docs.rs#370)    /// Adds a new chain to the list of chains smoldot tries to synchronize.
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    ///
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    /// Returns an error in case something is wrong with the configuration.
[373](https://docs.rs#373)    pub fn add_chain(
[374](https://docs.rs#374)        &mut self,
[375](https://docs.rs#375)        config: AddChainConfig<'_, TChain, impl Iterator<Item = ChainId>>,
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    ) -> Result<AddChainSuccess<TPlat>, AddChainError> {
[377](https://docs.rs#377)        // `chains_by_key` is created lazily whenever needed.
[378](https://docs.rs#378)        let chains_by_key = self.chains_by_key.get_or_insert_with(|| {
[379](https://docs.rs#379)            HashMap::with_hasher(util::SipHasherBuild::new({
[380](https://docs.rs#380)                let mut seed = [0; 16];
[381](https://docs.rs#381)                self.platform.fill_random_bytes(&mut seed);
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                seed
[383](https://docs.rs#383)            }))
[384](https://docs.rs#384)        });
[385](https://docs.rs#385)
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        // Decode the chain specification.
[387](https://docs.rs#387)        let chain_spec = match chain_spec::ChainSpec::from_json_bytes(config.specification) {
[388](https://docs.rs#388)            Ok(cs) => cs,
[389](https://docs.rs#389)            Err(err) => {
[390](https://docs.rs#390)                return Err(AddChainError::ChainSpecParseError(err));
[391](https://docs.rs#391)            }
[392](https://docs.rs#392)        };
[393](https://docs.rs#393)
[394](https://docs.rs#394)        // Build the genesis block, its hash, and information about the chain.
[395](https://docs.rs#395)        let (
[396](https://docs.rs#396)            genesis_chain_information,
[397](https://docs.rs#397)            genesis_block_header,
[398](https://docs.rs#398)            print_warning_genesis_root_chainspec,
[399](https://docs.rs#399)            genesis_block_state_root,
[400](https://docs.rs#400)        ) = {
[401](https://docs.rs#401)            // TODO: don't build the chain information if only the genesis hash is needed: https://github.com/smol-dot/smoldot/issues/1017
[402](https://docs.rs#402)            let genesis_chain_information = chain_spec.to_chain_information().map(|(ci, _)| ci); // TODO: don't just throw away the runtime;
[403](https://docs.rs#403)
[404](https://docs.rs#404)            match genesis_chain_information {
[405](https://docs.rs#405)                Ok(genesis_chain_information) => {
[406](https://docs.rs#406)                    let header = genesis_chain_information.as_ref().finalized_block_header;
[407](https://docs.rs#407)                    let state_root = *header.state_root;
[408](https://docs.rs#408)                    let scale_encoded =
[409](https://docs.rs#409)                        header.scale_encoding_vec(usize::from(chain_spec.block_number_bytes()));
[410](https://docs.rs#410)                    (
[411](https://docs.rs#411)                        Some(genesis_chain_information),
[412](https://docs.rs#412)                        scale_encoded,
[413](https://docs.rs#413)                        chain_spec.light_sync_state().is_some()
[414](https://docs.rs#414)                            || chain_spec.relay_chain().is_some(),
[415](https://docs.rs#415)                        state_root,
[416](https://docs.rs#416)                    )
[417](https://docs.rs#417)                }
[418](https://docs.rs#418)                Err(chain_spec::FromGenesisStorageError::UnknownStorageItems) => {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)                    let state_root = *chain_spec.genesis_storage().into_trie_root_hash().unwrap();
[420](https://docs.rs#420)                    let header = header::Header {
[421](https://docs.rs#421)                        parent_hash: [0; 32],
[422](https://docs.rs#422)                        number: 0,
[423](https://docs.rs#423)                        state_root,
[424](https://docs.rs#424)                        extrinsics_root: smoldot::trie::EMPTY_BLAKE2_TRIE_MERKLE_VALUE,
[425](https://docs.rs#425)                        digest: header::DigestRef::empty().into(),
[426](https://docs.rs#426)                    }
[427](https://docs.rs#427)                    .scale_encoding_vec(usize::from(chain_spec.block_number_bytes()));
[428](https://docs.rs#428)                    (None, header, false, state_root)
[429](https://docs.rs#429)                }
[430](https://docs.rs#430)                Err(err) => return Err(AddChainError::InvalidGenesisStorage(err)),
[431](https://docs.rs#431)            }
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        };
[433](https://docs.rs#433)        let genesis_block_hash = header::hash_from_scale_encoded_header(&genesis_block_header);
[434](https://docs.rs#434)
[435](https://docs.rs#435)        // Decode the database and make sure that it matches the chain by comparing the finalized
[436](https://docs.rs#436)        // block header in it with the actual one.
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        let (database, database_was_wrong_chain) = {
[438](https://docs.rs#438)            let mut maybe_database = database::decode_database(
[439](https://docs.rs#439)                config.database_content,
[440](https://docs.rs#440)                chain_spec.block_number_bytes().into(),
[441](https://docs.rs#441)            )
[442](https://docs.rs#442)            .ok();
[443](https://docs.rs#443)            let mut database_was_wrong = false;
[444](https://docs.rs#444)            if maybe_database
[445](https://docs.rs#445)                .as_ref()
[446](https://docs.rs#446)                .map_or(false, |db| db.genesis_block_hash != genesis_block_hash)
[447](https://docs.rs#447)            {
[448](https://docs.rs#448)                maybe_database = None;
[449](https://docs.rs#449)                database_was_wrong = true;
[450](https://docs.rs#450)            }
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            (maybe_database, database_was_wrong)
[452](https://docs.rs#452)        };
[453](https://docs.rs#453)
[454](https://docs.rs#454)        // Load the information about the chain. If a light sync state (also known as a checkpoint)
[455](https://docs.rs#455)        // is present in the chain spec, it is possible to start syncing at the finalized block
[456](https://docs.rs#456)        // it describes.
[457](https://docs.rs#457)        // At the same time, we deconstruct the database into `known_nodes`
[458](https://docs.rs#458)        // and `runtime_code_hint`.
[459](https://docs.rs#459)        let (chain_information, used_database_chain_information, known_nodes, runtime_code_hint) = {
[460](https://docs.rs#460)            let checkpoint = chain_spec
[461](https://docs.rs#461)                .light_sync_state()
[462](https://docs.rs#462)                .map(|s| s.to_chain_information());
[463](https://docs.rs#463)
[464](https://docs.rs#464)            match (genesis_chain_information, checkpoint, database) {
[465](https://docs.rs#465)                // Use the database if it contains a more recent block than the
[466](https://docs.rs#466)                // chain spec checkpoint.
[467](https://docs.rs#467)                (
[468](https://docs.rs#468)                    _,
[469](https://docs.rs#469)                    Some(Ok(checkpoint)),
[470](https://docs.rs#470)                    Some(database::DatabaseContent {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)                        chain_information: Some(db_ci),
[472](https://docs.rs#472)                        known_nodes,
[473](https://docs.rs#473)                        runtime_code_hint,
[474](https://docs.rs#474)                        ..
[475](https://docs.rs#475)                    }),
[476](https://docs.rs#476)                ) if db_ci.as_ref().finalized_block_header.number
[477](https://docs.rs#477)                    >= checkpoint.as_ref().finalized_block_header.number =>
[478](https://docs.rs#478)                {
[479](https://docs.rs#479)                    (Some(db_ci), true, known_nodes, runtime_code_hint)
[480](https://docs.rs#480)                }
[481](https://docs.rs#481)
[482](https://docs.rs#482)                // Otherwise, use the chain spec checkpoint.
[483](https://docs.rs#483)                (
[484](https://docs.rs#484)                    _,
[485](https://docs.rs#485)                    Some(Ok(checkpoint)),
[486](https://docs.rs#486)                    Some(database::DatabaseContent {
[487](https://docs.rs#487)                        known_nodes,
[488](https://docs.rs#488)                        runtime_code_hint,
[489](https://docs.rs#489)                        ..
[490](https://docs.rs#490)                    }),
[491](https://docs.rs#491)                ) => (Some(checkpoint), false, known_nodes, runtime_code_hint),
[492](https://docs.rs#492)                (_, Some(Ok(checkpoint)), None) => (Some(checkpoint), false, Vec::new(), None),
[493](https://docs.rs#493)
[494](https://docs.rs#494)                // If neither the genesis chain information nor the checkpoint chain information
[495](https://docs.rs#495)                // is available, we could in principle use the database, but for API reasons we
[496](https://docs.rs#496)                // don't want users to be able to rely on just a database (as we reserve the right
[497](https://docs.rs#497)                // to break the database at any point) and thus return an error.
[498](https://docs.rs#498)                (
[499](https://docs.rs#499)                    None,
[500](https://docs.rs#500)                    None,
[501](https://docs.rs#501)                    Some(database::DatabaseContent {
[502](https://docs.rs#502)                        known_nodes,
[503](https://docs.rs#503)                        runtime_code_hint,
[504](https://docs.rs#504)                        ..
[505](https://docs.rs#505)                    }),
[506](https://docs.rs#506)                ) => (None, false, known_nodes, runtime_code_hint),
[507](https://docs.rs#507)                (None, None, None) => (None, false, Vec::new(), None),
[508](https://docs.rs#508)
[509](https://docs.rs#509)                // Use the genesis block if no checkpoint is available.
[510](https://docs.rs#510)                (
[511](https://docs.rs#511)                    Some(genesis_ci),
[512](https://docs.rs#512)                    None
[513](https://docs.rs#513)                    | Some(Err(
[514](https://docs.rs#514)                        chain_spec::CheckpointToChainInformationError::GenesisBlockCheckpoint,
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                    )),
[516](https://docs.rs#516)                    Some(database::DatabaseContent {
[517](https://docs.rs#517)                        known_nodes,
[518](https://docs.rs#518)                        runtime_code_hint,
[519](https://docs.rs#519)                        ..
[520](https://docs.rs#520)                    }),
[521](https://docs.rs#521)                ) => (Some(genesis_ci), false, known_nodes, runtime_code_hint),
[522](https://docs.rs#522)                (
[523](https://docs.rs#523)                    Some(genesis_ci),
[524](https://docs.rs#524)                    None
[525](https://docs.rs#525)                    | Some(Err(
[526](https://docs.rs#526)                        chain_spec::CheckpointToChainInformationError::GenesisBlockCheckpoint,
[527](https://docs.rs#527)                    )),
[528](https://docs.rs#528)                    None,
[529](https://docs.rs#529)                ) => (Some(genesis_ci), false, Vec::new(), None),
[530](https://docs.rs#530)
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                // If the checkpoint format is invalid, we return an error no matter whether the
[532](https://docs.rs#532)                // genesis chain information could be used.
[533](https://docs.rs#533)                (_, Some(Err(err)), _) => {
[534](https://docs.rs#534)                    return Err(AddChainError::InvalidCheckpoint(err));
[535](https://docs.rs#535)                }
[536](https://docs.rs#536)            }
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        };
[538](https://docs.rs#538)
[539](https://docs.rs#539)        // If the chain specification specifies a parachain, find the corresponding relay chain
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        // in the list of potential relay chains passed by the user.
[541](https://docs.rs#541)        // If no relay chain can be found, the chain creation fails. Exactly one matching relay
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        // chain must be found. If there are multiple ones, the creation fails as well.
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        let relay_chain_id = if let Some((relay_chain_id, para_id)) = chain_spec.relay_chain() {
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            let chain = config
[545](https://docs.rs#545)                .potential_relay_chains
[546](https://docs.rs#546)                .filter(|c| {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)                    self.public_api_chains
[548](https://docs.rs#548)                        .get(c.0)
[549](https://docs.rs#549)                        .map_or(false, |chain| chain.chain_spec_chain_id == relay_chain_id)
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                })
[551](https://docs.rs#551)                .exactly_one();
[552](https://docs.rs#552)
[553](https://docs.rs#553)            match chain {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)                Ok(c) => Some((c, para_id)),
[555](https://docs.rs#555)                Err(mut iter) => {
[556](https://docs.rs#556)                    // `iter` here is identical to the iterator above before `exactly_one` is
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                    // called. This lets us know what failed.
[558](https://docs.rs#558)                    return Err(if iter.next().is_none() {
[559](https://docs.rs#559)                        AddChainError::NoRelayChainFound
[560](https://docs.rs#560)                    } else {
[561](https://docs.rs#561)                        debug_assert!(iter.next().is_some());
[562](https://docs.rs#562)                        AddChainError::MultipleRelayChains
[563](https://docs.rs#563)                    });
[564](https://docs.rs#564)                }
[565](https://docs.rs#565)            }
[566](https://docs.rs#566)        } else {
[567](https://docs.rs#567)            None
[568](https://docs.rs#568)        };
[569](https://docs.rs#569)
[570](https://docs.rs#570)        // Build the list of bootstrap nodes ahead of time.
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        // Because the specification of the format of a multiaddress is a bit flexible, it is
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        // not possible to firmly affirm that a multiaddress is invalid. For this reason, we
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        // simply ignore unparsable bootnode addresses rather than returning an error.
[574](https://docs.rs#574)        // A list of invalid bootstrap node addresses is kept in order to print a warning later
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        // in case it is non-empty. This list is sanitized in order to be safely printable as part
[576](https://docs.rs#576)        // of the logs.
[577](https://docs.rs#577)        let (bootstrap_nodes, invalid_bootstrap_nodes_sanitized) = {
[578](https://docs.rs#578)            let mut valid_list = Vec::with_capacity(chain_spec.boot_nodes().len());
[579](https://docs.rs#579)            let mut invalid_list = Vec::with_capacity(0);
[580](https://docs.rs#580)            for node in chain_spec.boot_nodes() {
[581](https://docs.rs#581)                match node {
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                    chain_spec::Bootnode::Parsed { multiaddr, peer_id } => {
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                        if let Ok(multiaddr) = multiaddr.parse::<multiaddr::Multiaddr>() {
[584](https://docs.rs#584)                            let peer_id = peer_id::PeerId::from_bytes(peer_id).unwrap();
[585](https://docs.rs#585)                            valid_list.push((peer_id, vec![multiaddr]));
[586](https://docs.rs#586)                        } else {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                            invalid_list.push(multiaddr)
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                        }
[589](https://docs.rs#589)                    }
[590](https://docs.rs#590)                    chain_spec::Bootnode::UnrecognizedFormat(unparsed) => invalid_list.push(
[591](https://docs.rs#591)                        unparsed
[592](https://docs.rs#592)                            .chars()
[593](https://docs.rs#593)                            .filter(|c| c.is_ascii())
[594](https://docs.rs#594)                            .collect::<String>(),
[595](https://docs.rs#595)                    ),
[596](https://docs.rs#596)                }
[597](https://docs.rs#597)            }
[598](https://docs.rs#598)            (valid_list, invalid_list)
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        };
[600](https://docs.rs#600)
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        // All the checks are performed above. Adding the chain can't fail anymore at this point.
[602](https://docs.rs#602)
[603](https://docs.rs#603)        // Grab this field from the chain specification for later, as the chain specification is
[604](https://docs.rs#604)        // consumed below.
[605](https://docs.rs#605)        let chain_spec_chain_id = chain_spec.id().to_owned();
[606](https://docs.rs#606)
[607](https://docs.rs#607)        // The key generated here uniquely identifies this chain within smoldot. Multiple chains
[608](https://docs.rs#608)        // having the same key will use the same services.
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        //
[610](https://docs.rs#610)        // This struct is extremely important from a security perspective. We want multiple
[611](https://docs.rs#611)        // identical chains to be de-duplicated, but security issues would arise if two chains
[612](https://docs.rs#612)        // were considered identical while they're in reality not identical.
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        let new_chain_key = ChainKey {
[614](https://docs.rs#614)            genesis_block_hash,
[615](https://docs.rs#615)            relay_chain: relay_chain_id.map(|(ck, _)| {
[616](https://docs.rs#616)                (
[617](https://docs.rs#617)                    Box::new(self.public_api_chains.get(ck.0).unwrap().key.clone()),
[618](https://docs.rs#618)                    chain_spec.relay_chain().unwrap().1,
[619](https://docs.rs#619)                )
[620](https://docs.rs#620)            }),
[621](https://docs.rs#621)            fork_id: chain_spec.fork_id().map(|f| f.to_owned()),
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        };
[623](https://docs.rs#623)
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        // If the chain we are adding is a parachain, grab the services of the relay chain.
[625](https://docs.rs#625)        //
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        // This could in principle be done later on, but doing so raises borrow checker errors.
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        let relay_chain: Option<(ChainServices<_>, u32, String)> =
[628](https://docs.rs#628)            relay_chain_id.map(|(relay_chain, para_id)| {
[629](https://docs.rs#629)                let relay_chain = &chains_by_key
[630](https://docs.rs#630)                    .get(&self.public_api_chains.get(relay_chain.0).unwrap().key)
[631](https://docs.rs#631)                    .unwrap();
[632](https://docs.rs#632)                (
[633](https://docs.rs#633)                    relay_chain.services.clone(),
[634](https://docs.rs#634)                    para_id,
[635](https://docs.rs#635)                    relay_chain.log_name.clone(),
[636](https://docs.rs#636)                )
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            });
[638](https://docs.rs#638)
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        // Determinate the name under which the chain will be identified in the logs.
[640](https://docs.rs#640)        // Because the chain spec is untrusted input, we must transform the `id` to remove all
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        // weird characters.
[642](https://docs.rs#642)        //
[643](https://docs.rs#643)        // By default, this log name will be equal to chain's `id`. Since it is possible for
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        // multiple different chains to have the same `id`, we need to look into the list of
[645](https://docs.rs#645)        // existing chains and make sure that there's no conflict, in which case the log name
[646](https://docs.rs#646)        // will have the suffix `-1`, or `-2`, or `-3`, and so on.
[647](https://docs.rs#647)        //
[648](https://docs.rs#648)        // This value is ignored if we enter the `Entry::Occupied` block below. Because the
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        // calculation requires accessing the list of existing chains, this block can't be put in
[650](https://docs.rs#650)        // the `Entry::Vacant` block below, even though it would make more sense for it to be
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        // there.
[652](https://docs.rs#652)        let log_name = {
[653](https://docs.rs#653)            let base = chain_spec
[654](https://docs.rs#654)                .id()
[655](https://docs.rs#655)                .chars()
[656](https://docs.rs#656)                .filter(|c| c.is_ascii_graphic())
[657](https://docs.rs#657)                .collect::<String>();
[658](https://docs.rs#658)            let mut suffix = None;
[659](https://docs.rs#659)
[660](https://docs.rs#660)            loop {
[661](https://docs.rs#661)                let attempt = if let Some(suffix) = suffix {
[662](https://docs.rs#662)                    format!("{base}-{suffix}")
[663](https://docs.rs#663)                } else {
[664](https://docs.rs#664)                    base.clone()
[665](https://docs.rs#665)                };
[666](https://docs.rs#666)
[667](https://docs.rs#667)                if !chains_by_key.values().any(|c| *c.log_name == attempt) {
[668](https://docs.rs#668)                    break attempt;
[669](https://docs.rs#669)                }
[670](https://docs.rs#670)
[671](https://docs.rs#671)                match &mut suffix {
[672](https://docs.rs#672)                    Some(v) => *v += 1,
[673](https://docs.rs#673)                    v @ None => *v = Some(1),
[674](https://docs.rs#674)                }
[675](https://docs.rs#675)            }
[676](https://docs.rs#676)        };
[677](https://docs.rs#677)
[678](https://docs.rs#678)        let statement_protocol_config = config.statement_protocol_config;
[679](https://docs.rs#679)
[680](https://docs.rs#680)        let max_seen_statements = statement_protocol_config
[681](https://docs.rs#681)            .as_ref()
[682](https://docs.rs#682)            .map(|c| c.max_seen_statements());
[683](https://docs.rs#683)
[684](https://docs.rs#684)        // Start the services of the chain to add, or grab the services if they already exist.
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        let (services, log_name) = match chains_by_key.entry(new_chain_key.clone()) {
[686](https://docs.rs#686)            Entry::Occupied(mut entry) => {
[687](https://docs.rs#687)                // The chain to add always has a corresponding chain running. Simply grab the
[688](https://docs.rs#688)                // existing services and existing log name.
[689](https://docs.rs#689)                // The `log_name` created above is discarded in favour of the existing log name.
[690](https://docs.rs#690)                entry.get_mut().num_references = entry.get().num_references.checked_add(1).unwrap();
[691](https://docs.rs#691)                let entry = entry.into_mut();
[692](https://docs.rs#692)                (&mut entry.services, &entry.log_name)
[693](https://docs.rs#693)            }
[694](https://docs.rs#694)            Entry::Vacant(entry) => {
[695](https://docs.rs#695)                if let (None, None) = (&relay_chain, &chain_information) {
[696](https://docs.rs#696)                    return Err(AddChainError::ChainSpecNeitherGenesisStorageNorCheckpoint);
[697](https://docs.rs#697)                }
[698](https://docs.rs#698)
[699](https://docs.rs#699)                // Start the services of the new chain.
[700](https://docs.rs#700)                let services = {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)                    // Version of the client when requested through the networking.
[702](https://docs.rs#702)                    let network_identify_agent_version = format!(
[703](https://docs.rs#703)                        "{} {}",
[704](https://docs.rs#704)                        self.platform.client_name(),
[705](https://docs.rs#705)                        self.platform.client_version()
[706](https://docs.rs#706)                    );
[707](https://docs.rs#707)
[708](https://docs.rs#708)                    let config = match (&relay_chain, &chain_information) {
[709](https://docs.rs#709)                        (Some((relay_chain, para_id, _)), _) => StartServicesChainTy::Parachain {
[710](https://docs.rs#710)                            relay_chain,
[711](https://docs.rs#711)                            para_id: *para_id,
[712](https://docs.rs#712)                        },
[713](https://docs.rs#713)                        (None, Some(chain_information)) => {
[714](https://docs.rs#714)                            StartServicesChainTy::SubstrateCompatible { chain_information }
[715](https://docs.rs#715)                        }
[716](https://docs.rs#716)                        (None, None) => {
[717](https://docs.rs#717)                            // Checked above.
[718](https://docs.rs#718)                            unreachable!()
[719](https://docs.rs#719)                        }
[720](https://docs.rs#720)                    };
[721](https://docs.rs#721)
[722](https://docs.rs#722)                    start_services(
[723](https://docs.rs#723)                        log_name.clone(),

[726](https://docs.rs#726)                        runtime_code_hint,

[889](https://docs.rs#889)        if bootstrap_nodes.is_empty() {
[890](https://docs.rs#890)            // Note the usage of the word "likely", because another chain with the same key might
[891](https://docs.rs#891)            // have been added earlier and contains bootnodes, or we might receive an incoming
[892](https://docs.rs#892)            // substream on a connection normally used for a different chain.
[893](https://docs.rs#893)            log!(

[896](https://docs.rs#896)                "smoldot",

[898](https://docs.rs#898)                    "Newly-added chain {} has an empty list of bootnodes. Smoldot will \
[899](https://docs.rs#899)                    likely fail to connect to its peer-to-peer network.",
[900](https://docs.rs#900)                    log_name
[901](https://docs.rs#901)                )
[902](https://docs.rs#902)            );
[903](https://docs.rs#903)        }
[904](https://docs.rs#904)
[905](https://docs.rs#905)        // Apart from its services, each chain also has an entry in `public_api_chains`.
[906](https://docs.rs#906)        let public_api_chains_entry = self.public_api_chains.vacant_entry();
[907](https://docs.rs#907)        let new_chain_id = ChainId(public_api_chains_entry.key());
[908](https://docs.rs#908)
[909](https://docs.rs#909)        // Multiple chains can share the same network service, but each specify different
[910](https://docs.rs#910)        // bootstrap nodes and database nodes. In order to resolve this, each chain adds their own
[911](https://docs.rs#911)        // bootnodes and database nodes to the network service after it has been initialized. This
[912](https://docs.rs#912)        // is done by adding a short-lived task that waits for the chain initialization to finish
[913](https://docs.rs#913)        // then adds the nodes.
[914](https://docs.rs#914)        self.platform
[915](https://docs.rs#915)            .spawn_task("network-service-add-initial-topology".into(), {
[916](https://docs.rs#916)                let network_service = services.network_service.clone();
[917](https://docs.rs#917)                async move {
[918](https://docs.rs#918)                    network_service.discover(known_nodes, false).await;
[919](https://docs.rs#919)                    network_service.discover(bootstrap_nodes, true).await;
[920](https://docs.rs#920)                }
[921](https://docs.rs#921)            });
[922](https://docs.rs#922)
[923](https://docs.rs#923)        // JSON-RPC service initialization. This is done every time `add_chain` is called, even
[924](https://docs.rs#924)        // if a similar chain already existed.
[925](https://docs.rs#925)        let json_rpc_frontend = if let AddChainConfigJsonRpc::Enabled {
[926](https://docs.rs#926)            max_pending_requests,
[927](https://docs.rs#927)            max_subscriptions,
[928](https://docs.rs#928)        } = config.json_rpc
[929](https://docs.rs#929)        {
[930](https://docs.rs#930)            let frontend = json_rpc_service::service(json_rpc_service::Config {
[931](https://docs.rs#931)                platform: self.platform.clone(),
[932](https://docs.rs#932)                log_name: log_name.clone(), // TODO: add a way to differentiate multiple different json-rpc services under the same chain
[933](https://docs.rs#933)                max_pending_requests,
[934](https://docs.rs#934)                max_subscriptions,
[935](https://docs.rs#935)                sync_service: services.sync_service.clone(),
[936](https://docs.rs#936)                network_service: services.network_service.clone(),
[937](https://docs.rs#937)                transactions_service: services.transactions_service.clone(),
[938](https://docs.rs#938)                runtime_service: services.runtime_service.clone(),
[939](https://docs.rs#939)                bitswap_service: services.bitswap_service.clone(),
[940](https://docs.rs#940)                chain_name: chain_spec.name().to_owned(),
[941](https://docs.rs#941)                chain_ty: chain_spec.chain_type().to_owned(),
[942](https://docs.rs#942)                chain_is_live: chain_spec.has_live_network(),
[943](https://docs.rs#943)                chain_properties_json: chain_spec.properties().to_owned(),
[944](https://docs.rs#944)                system_name: self.platform.client_name().into_owned(),
[945](https://docs.rs#945)                system_version: self.platform.client_version().into_owned(),
[946](https://docs.rs#946)                genesis_block_hash,
[947](https://docs.rs#947)                statement_protocol_config,
[948](https://docs.rs#948)                max_seen_statements,
[949](https://docs.rs#949)            });
[950](https://docs.rs#950)
[951](https://docs.rs#951)            Some(frontend)
[952](https://docs.rs#952)        } else {
[953](https://docs.rs#953)            None
[954](https://docs.rs#954)        };
[955](https://docs.rs#955)
[956](https://docs.rs#956)        // Success!
[957](https://docs.rs#957)        let public_api_chain_destroyed_event = event_listener::Event::new();
[958](https://docs.rs#958)        let public_api_chain_destroyed = public_api_chain_destroyed_event.listen();
[959](https://docs.rs#959)        public_api_chains_entry.insert(PublicApiChain {
[960](https://docs.rs#960)            user_data: config.user_data,
[961](https://docs.rs#961)            key: new_chain_key,
[962](https://docs.rs#962)            chain_spec_chain_id,
[963](https://docs.rs#963)            json_rpc_frontend: json_rpc_frontend.clone(),
[964](https://docs.rs#964)            public_api_chain_destroyed_event,
[965](https://docs.rs#965)        });
[966](https://docs.rs#966)        Ok(AddChainSuccess {
[967](https://docs.rs#967)            chain_id: new_chain_id,
[968](https://docs.rs#968)            json_rpc_responses: json_rpc_frontend.map(|f| JsonRpcResponses {
[969](https://docs.rs#969)                inner: Some(f),
[970](https://docs.rs#970)                public_api_chain_destroyed,
[971](https://docs.rs#971)            }),
[972](https://docs.rs#972)        })
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    }
[974](https://docs.rs#974)
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    /// Removes the chain from smoldot. This instantaneously and silently cancels all on-going
[976](https://docs.rs#976)    /// JSON-RPC requests and subscriptions.
[977](https://docs.rs#977)    ///
[978](https://docs.rs#978)    /// The provided [`ChainId`] is now considered dead. Be aware that this same [`ChainId`] might
[979](https://docs.rs#979)    /// later be reused if [`Client::add_chain`] is called again.
[980](https://docs.rs#980)    ///
[981](https://docs.rs#981)    /// While from the API perspective it will look like the chain no longer exists, calling this
[982](https://docs.rs#982)    /// function will not actually immediately disconnect from the given chain if it is still used
[983](https://docs.rs#983)    /// as the relay chain of a parachain.
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    ///
[985](https://docs.rs#985)    /// If the [`JsonRpcResponses`] object that was returned when adding the chain is still alive,
[986](https://docs.rs#986)    /// [`JsonRpcResponses::next`] will now return `None`.
[987](https://docs.rs#987)    #[must_use]
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    pub fn remove_chain(&mut self, id: ChainId) -> TChain {
[989](https://docs.rs#989)        let removed_chain = self.public_api_chains.remove(id.0);
[990](https://docs.rs#990)
[991](https://docs.rs#991)        removed_chain
[992](https://docs.rs#992)            .public_api_chain_destroyed_event
[993](https://docs.rs#993)            .notify(usize::MAX);
[994](https://docs.rs#994)
[995](https://docs.rs#995)        // `chains_by_key` is created lazily when `add_chain` is called.
[996](https://docs.rs#996)        // Since we're removing a chain that has been added with `add_chain`, it is guaranteed
[997](https://docs.rs#997)        // that `chains_by_key` is set.
[998](https://docs.rs#998)        let chains_by_key = self
[999](https://docs.rs#999)            .chains_by_key
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)            .as_mut()
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)            .unwrap_or_else(|| unreachable!());
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)        let running_chain = chains_by_key.get_mut(&removed_chain.key).unwrap();
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)        if running_chain.num_references.get() == 1 {
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)            log!(
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)                &self.platform,
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)                Info,
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)                "smoldot",
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)                format!("Shutting down chain {}", running_chain.log_name)
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)            );
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)            chains_by_key.remove(&removed_chain.key);
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)        } else {
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)            running_chain.num_references =
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)                NonZero::<u32>::new(running_chain.num_references.get() - 1).unwrap();
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)        }
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)        self.public_api_chains.shrink_to_fit();
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)        removed_chain.user_data
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)    }
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)    /// Enqueues a JSON-RPC request towards the given chain.
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)    ///
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)    /// Since most JSON-RPC requests can only be answered asynchronously, the request is only
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)    /// queued and will be decoded and processed later.
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)    ///
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)    /// Returns an error if the number of requests that have been sent but whose answer hasn't been
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)    /// pulled with [`JsonRpcResponses::next`] is superior or equal to the value that was passed
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)    /// through [`AddChainConfigJsonRpc::Enabled::max_pending_requests`]. In that situation, the
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)    /// API user is encouraged to stop sending requests and start pulling answers with
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)    /// [`JsonRpcResponses::next`].
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)    ///
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)    /// Passing `u32::MAX` to [`AddChainConfigJsonRpc::Enabled::max_pending_requests`] is
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)    /// a good way to avoid errors here, but this should only be done if the JSON-RPC client is
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)    /// trusted.
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)    ///
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)    /// If the JSON-RPC request is not a valid JSON-RPC request, a JSON-RPC error response with
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)    /// an `id` equal to `null` is later generated, in accordance with the JSON-RPC specification.
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)    ///
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)    /// # Panic
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)    ///
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)    /// Panics if the [`ChainId`] is invalid, or if [`AddChainConfig::json_rpc`] was
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)    /// [`AddChainConfigJsonRpc::Disabled`] when adding the chain.
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)    ///
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)    pub fn json_rpc_request(
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)        &mut self,
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)        json_rpc_request: impl Into<String>,
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)        chain_id: ChainId,
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)    ) -> Result<(), HandleRpcError> {
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)        self.json_rpc_request_inner(json_rpc_request.into(), chain_id)
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)    }
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)    fn json_rpc_request_inner(
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)        &mut self,
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)        json_rpc_request: String,
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)        chain_id: ChainId,
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)    ) -> Result<(), HandleRpcError> {
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)        let json_rpc_sender = match self
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)            .public_api_chains
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)            .get_mut(chain_id.0)
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)            .unwrap()
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)            .json_rpc_frontend
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)        {
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)            Some(ref mut json_rpc_sender) => json_rpc_sender,
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)            _ => panic!(),
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)        };
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)        json_rpc_sender.queue_rpc_request(json_rpc_request)
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)    }
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)}

[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)/// Error potentially returned by [`Client::add_chain`].
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)#[derive(Debug, derive_more::Display, derive_more::Error)]
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)pub enum AddChainError {
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)    /// Failed to decode the specification of the chain.
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)    #[display("Failed to decode chain specification: {_0}")]
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)    ChainSpecParseError(chain_spec::ParseError),
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)    /// The chain specification must contain either the storage of the genesis block, or a
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)    /// checkpoint. Neither was provided.
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)    #[display("Either a checkpoint or the genesis storage must be provided")]
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)    ChainSpecNeitherGenesisStorageNorCheckpoint,
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)    /// Checkpoint provided in the chain specification is invalid.
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)    #[display("Invalid checkpoint in chain specification: {_0}")]
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)    InvalidCheckpoint(chain_spec::CheckpointToChainInformationError),
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)    /// Failed to build the information about the chain from the genesis storage. This indicates
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)    /// invalid data in the genesis storage.
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)    #[display("Failed to build genesis chain information: {_0}")]
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)    InvalidGenesisStorage(chain_spec::FromGenesisStorageError),
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)    /// The list of potential relay chains doesn't contain any relay chain with the name indicated
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)    /// in the chain specification of the parachain.
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)    #[display("Couldn't find relevant relay chain")]
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)    NoRelayChainFound,
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)    /// The list of potential relay chains contains more than one relay chain with the name
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)    /// indicated in the chain specification of the parachain.
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)    #[display("Multiple relevant relay chains found")]
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)    MultipleRelayChains,
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)}

[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)/// Starts all the services of the client.
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)///
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)/// Returns some of the services that have been started. If these service get shut down, all the
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)/// other services will later shut down as well.
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)fn start_services<TPlat: platform::PlatformRef>(
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)    log_name: String,
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)    platform: &TPlat,
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)    network_service: &mut Option<Arc<network_service::NetworkService<TPlat>>>,
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)    runtime_code_hint: Option<database::DatabaseContentRuntimeCodeHint>,
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)    genesis_block_scale_encoded_header: Vec<u8>,
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)    block_number_bytes: usize,
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)    fork_id: Option<String>,
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)    config: StartServicesChainTy<'_, TPlat>,
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)    network_identify_agent_version: String,
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)    statement_protocol_config: Option<network_service::StatementProtocolConfig>,
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)) -> ChainServices<TPlat> {
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)    let network_service = network_service.get_or_insert_with(|| {
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)        network_service::NetworkService::new(network_service::Config {
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)            platform: platform.clone(),
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)            identify_agent_version: network_identify_agent_version,
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)            connections_open_pool_size: 8,
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)            connections_open_pool_restore_delay: Duration::from_millis(100),
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)            chains_capacity: 1,
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)        })
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)    });
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)    let network_service_chain = network_service.add_chain(network_service::ConfigChain {
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)        log_name: log_name.clone(),
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)        num_out_slots: 4,
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)        grandpa_protocol_finalized_block_height: match &config {
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)            StartServicesChainTy::SubstrateCompatible { chain_information }
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)                if matches!(
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)                    chain_information.as_ref().finality,
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)                    chain::chain_information::ChainInformationFinalityRef::Grandpa { .. }
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)                ) =>
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)            {
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)                Some(chain_information.as_ref().finalized_block_header.number)
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)            }
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)            _ => None,
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)        },
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)        genesis_block_hash: header::hash_from_scale_encoded_header(
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)            &genesis_block_scale_encoded_header,
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)        ),
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)        best_block: match &config {
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)            StartServicesChainTy::SubstrateCompatible { chain_information } => (
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)                chain_information.as_ref().finalized_block_header.number,
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)                chain_information
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)                    .as_ref()
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)                    .finalized_block_header
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)                    .hash(block_number_bytes),
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)            ),
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)            _ => (
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)                0,
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)                header::hash_from_scale_encoded_header(&genesis_block_scale_encoded_header),
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)            ),
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)        },
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)        fork_id,
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)        block_number_bytes,
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)        statement_protocol_config,
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)    });
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)    let (sync_service, runtime_service) = match config {
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)        StartServicesChainTy::Parachain {
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)            relay_chain,
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)            para_id,
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)        } => {
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)            // Chain is a parachain.
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)            // The sync service is leveraging the network service, downloads block headers,
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)            // and verifies them, to determine what are the best and finalized blocks of the
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)            // chain.
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)            let sync_service = Arc::new(sync_service::SyncService::new(sync_service::Config {
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)                platform: platform.clone(),
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)                log_name: log_name.clone(),
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)                block_number_bytes,
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)                network_service: network_service_chain.clone(),
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)                chain_type: sync_service::ConfigChainType::Parachain(
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)                    sync_service::ConfigParachain {
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)                        relay_chain: sync_service::ConfigRelayChain {
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)                            para_id,
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)                            relay_chain_sync: relay_chain.runtime_service.clone(),
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)                        },
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)                    },
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)                ),
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)            }));
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)            // The runtime service follows the runtime of the best block of the chain,
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)            // and allows performing runtime calls.
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)            let runtime_service = Arc::new(runtime_service::RuntimeService::new(
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)                runtime_service::Config {
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)                    log_name: log_name.clone(),
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)                    platform: platform.clone(),
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)                    sync_service: sync_service.clone(),
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)                    network_service: network_service_chain.clone(),
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)                    genesis_block_scale_encoded_header,
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)                },
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)            ));
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)            (sync_service, runtime_service)
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)        }
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)        StartServicesChainTy::SubstrateCompatible { chain_information } => {
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)            // Chain is a Substrate-compatible non-parachain chain.
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)            // The sync service is leveraging the network service, downloads block headers,
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)            // and verifies them, to determine what are the best and finalized blocks of the
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)            // chain.
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)            let sync_service = Arc::new(sync_service::SyncService::new(sync_service::Config {
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)                log_name: log_name.clone(),
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)                block_number_bytes,
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)                platform: platform.clone(),
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)                network_service: network_service_chain.clone(),
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)                chain_type: sync_service::ConfigChainType::SubstrateCompatible(
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)                    sync_service::ConfigSubstrateCompatible {
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)                        chain_information: chain_information.clone(),
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)                        runtime_code_hint: runtime_code_hint.map(|hint| {
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)                            sync_service::ConfigSubstrateCompatibleRuntimeCodeHint {
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)                                storage_value: hint.code,
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)                                merkle_value: hint.code_merkle_value,
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)                                closest_ancestor_excluding: hint.closest_ancestor_excluding,
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)                            }
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)                        }),
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)                    },
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)                ),
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)            }));
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)            // The runtime service follows the runtime of the best block of the chain,
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)            // and allows performing runtime calls.
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)            let runtime_service = Arc::new(runtime_service::RuntimeService::new(
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)                runtime_service::Config {
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)                    log_name: log_name.clone(),
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)                    platform: platform.clone(),
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)                    sync_service: sync_service.clone(),
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)                    network_service: network_service_chain.clone(),
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)                    genesis_block_scale_encoded_header,
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)                },
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)            ));
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)            (sync_service, runtime_service)
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)        }
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)    };
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)    // The transactions service lets one send transactions to the peer-to-peer network and watch
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)    // them being included in the chain.
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)    // While this service is in principle not needed if it is known ahead of time that no
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)    // transaction will be submitted, the service itself is pretty low cost.
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)    let transactions_service = Arc::new(transactions_service::TransactionsService::new(
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)        transactions_service::Config {
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)            log_name: log_name.clone(),
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)            platform: platform.clone(),
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)            sync_service: sync_service.clone(),
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)            runtime_service: runtime_service.clone(),
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)            network_service: network_service_chain.clone(),
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)            max_pending_transactions: NonZero::<u32>::new(64).unwrap(),
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)            max_concurrent_downloads: NonZero::<u32>::new(3).unwrap(),
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)            max_concurrent_validations: NonZero::<u32>::new(2).unwrap(),
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)        },
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)    ));
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)    // The Bitswap service fulfils `bitswap_unstable_get(cid)` and `bitswap_unstable_stream(cids)`
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)    // JSON-RPC requests by querying remote nodes for IPFS blocks.
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)    let bitswap_service = Arc::new(bitswap_service::BitswapService::new(
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)        bitswap_service::Config {
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)            log_name,
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)            platform: platform.clone(),
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)            network_service: network_service_chain.clone(),
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)        },
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)    ));
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)    ChainServices {
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)        network_service: network_service_chain,
